reasoning: Both sets are detailed and close in quality. They share the same tooling conventions, and both wrongly route Sharadar through Nasdaq Data Link instead of api.sharadar.com. A is more faithful on Stage 1. It has the yahooquery cross-check (XCHK-01 to XCHK-05) and the user's 10-name delisted reference check (CHECK-09). Its M1 walking skeleton is a true vertical slice: the app starts a download, shows live WebSocket progress, then search, company page and universe, all on generated OpenAPI types. Every later stage opens with a synthetic known-answer skeleton milestone (M4, M6, M8) before the real-data milestone, and RF-03 stays on S4 as the user specified. A also ships CONSTRAINTS.md. A has two real faults. It drops the PPO agents from S4 ('Learned allocation agents (PPO) are a separate, later idea'), and it ignores the rented GPU (QR-11 trains 'on the user's Apple Silicon laptop, locally'). Its brief is still framed around Stage 1 only. B covers the whole project: PPO agents with a budget, GPU rental, a central hypothesis ledger, one shared walk-forward schedule with a purge gap and a lockbox, and a full-project brief. But it leaves out the Yahoo cross-check and the user's delisted reference list entirely, and adds FRED and EDGAR instead. Its S2 has no synthetic skeleton: M4 depends on M3's real data and bundles the shared engine with the covariance study. M8 lumps forecast portfolios, agents and the verdict together. RF-03 is pushed into S3, the M1 app slice is thin (membership page only), and CONSTRAINTS.md is missing even though every packet cites it. Overall, A wins narrowly on milestone structure, Stage 1 fidelity and reference use. B wins on stage completeness.
